trickyParts: The divisor is the replica count SQUARED because the fan-out makes one accepted reread cost a store read on every pod. Anyone re-sizing these buckets has to size them against the store's budget, not against the HTTP rate: red row 7 measures the per-reread cost against two real processes and then does the arithmetic on the live limits, which is why it cannot be satisfied by restating a constant, and its two budget figures are deliberately written in the row rather than read from internal/broker/api.

The listener and the five-minute reload run on context.WithoutCancel of the signal's context, so the order at shutdown is a dependency: endServing() stops the loops, and only then st.Close() releases the store the listener dials through.

One boot behaviour changes with that: the first policy load and the OAuth secret's read no longer end early on a signal that arrives while they run, so a pod signalled mid-boot finishes them and then drains. policy.NewCurrent's own contract is intact — its loop logs no failed-load line once its context has ended, which is now the end of the shutdown rather than the signal, so the line a deployment alarms on still counts only loads that failed while the broker was meant to be serving.

A broker now waits up to rereadListenWait (5 s) for its first LISTEN dial before it binds. A dial that fails answers that wait as fast as one that succeeds, so a pod whose database takes no LISTEN connection still boots and still serves, as the plan requires; what the wait buys is that an address the load balancer can reach is an address a retag can reach.
deviations: Two defects beyond the tester's two were found while making row 8 pass reliably, and both are fixed here rather than reported. (a) oauthStore.Secret ran on the signal's context after the bind, so a SIGTERM arriving between the bind and the end of boot killed the process with fatal() and 'store OAuth provider secret: context canceled' where its callers saw a reset connection; it now runs on the serving context and such a pod drains. Row 8 failed roughly half the time on this before the fix and 5/5 after it. (b) A pod logged 'broker listening' and began serving before its first LISTEN dial returned, a 12-16 ms window in which a peer's notification reached a channel nobody on this pod was on yet; the bind now waits for that dial. Both were found with a go build overlay over a scratch copy of main.go, with the repository untouched.

Three pre-existing rows in internal/broker/api/handlers_secrets_test.go went red on the new burst of 2. They are about what a reread answers, not about sizing, so each now injects its own broker-wide bucket through the file's existing convention (newTestServerWith with d.RereadOverallLimit), keeping every assertion it had. Nothing was weakened, skipped or deleted, and neither of the tester's red rows was touched.
openQuestions: None. The architect ruled on both failures: fix both, state the quota the same way in all four places, and let the listener and the reload outlive the signal.
discoveredComplexity: store.Close had no caller outside tests, as the tester noted; the shutdown path that now ends the listener and the reload is where it belongs, and it is called there.

The burst of 2 is the first figure a person meets: agent-secrets secret writing several secrets at once is refused broker-wide after two of them, with Retry-After 1 s (4 s on Secret Manager). The write stands in the store either way and only the narrowing of who may read it waits for the next token; this is stated in limits.go, operate.md, the troubleshooting guide and the pull request body, because it is a behaviour change an operator and a person will both notice.
